question: Can a precommitted vector-dependent search over rational curves through both lifted public points produce rational relations on fresh public queries, with every candidate and reject counted?
base_curve: E/F_p: y^2=x^3-x-2; exact G and prime subgroup q from pinned registry
target_law: for j=0,1,2,3, w=1+SHA256('xedni-vector-shift-v1|p|j') interpreted big-endian modulo q-1; Q=wG; fixture construction is outside candidate search
query_law: offsets [0,1,2,3,5,8,13,21]; first 16 lexicographic ordered distinct offsets per target with both U=Q-t1G and V=Q-t2G nonidentity
candidate_law: for each query and selected vector (a,b), take centered affine coordinates (x1,y1),(x2,y2) of U,V and enumerate four vector-dependent shift tuples (dx1,dy1,dx2,dy2): (0,0,0,0), (a,0,0,0), (0,b,0,0), (a,b,-a,-b). Lift to (xi+p*dxi,yi+p*dyi). When lifted x differ, solve the two short-Weierstrass point equations exactly for rational A,B. Require nonsingularity and good integral reduction to A=-1,B=-2 at p. Test the rational relation aP+bQ=O only after both public points have been lifted.
workload: 8 fields times 4 targets times 16 queries times 13 vectors times 4 candidate shifts = 26624 construction attempts in fixed field,target,query,vector,shift order
controls: for each field, separately test the exact rational curve y^2=x^3-x-2 with P=(2,2), Q=2P and vector (2,-1) as a positive relation control, and Q=3P as a negative relation control; these 16 controls are outside the candidate workload
statuses: retain same_x, nonintegral, singular, invalid_point, bad_reduction, rational_relation, no_rational_relation and producer_failure with all attempted candidates; never drop failed or censored rows
diagnostic: compute the public aU+bV=O event after each rational candidate test; compare the candidate success set with the public relation set and record both without using the diagnostic to select curves
measurement: exact correctness and candidate-operation panel on local host; no isolated wall-time comparison
formal_goal: for an arbitrary indexed family of rational additive groups, compatible reduction maps, points and coefficient vectors, show that existence of any rational relation implies a public relation in that same vector; retain exact map and point-matching hypotheses
